messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Supplier boarding: GrowthPay initial intake & PO/ACH details

Hi Alicia,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood — excited to get GrowthPay set up so we can start routing PO'd spend. To move the vendor record through procurement and allow us to issue POs, could you send the following items at your earliest convenience: 

- Legal entity name (exactly as it appears on W-9)
- Company address (registered/incorporation and remit-to if different)
- Federal Tax ID / EIN (or W-8 classification if non-US)
- W-9 (PDF) or W-8BEN/W-8BEN-E if applicable
- Remit-to details: ACH account + routing (we accept ACH for US vendors) or wire instructions
- Bank letter or voided check (to validate ACH)
- Contact for invoices and PO reconciliation (name, email, phone)
- Any vendor portal preference for invoicing (email or EDI)

I've attached our buyer intake template (redwood_buyer_intake_v1.xlsx) and a short procurement kickoff checklist. Typical lead time: once we have completed docs and bank validation, vendor activation and PO issuance is usually 5–7 business days. If you have an urgent upcoming invoice, let us know the invoice date/amount and we'll prioritize.

A few process notes to avoid delays:
- Remit-to name must match legal entity on the W-9 to pass our finance validations.
- For ACH, we require a bank letter or voided check for verification.
- Redwood issues POs for orders > $5,000; for smaller one-offs we can accept invoices without a PO but will need payment terms confirmed.

If you prefer, Marcus (copied) can run a quick phone call to walk through the intake form.

Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Procurement Partner | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0126

Awesome — thanks for the quick turnaround and attachments, Alicia. Confirmed receipt of bank letter and authorization. A few clarifications: 

- Yes, include the Redwood PO number on the invoice in the PO field and add any project code in the invoice description; that makes reconciliation much faster.
- When you upload the W-9 please ensure the "legal name" field matches the EIN you provided. If the remit-to account name differs from the legal name, please indicate that explicitly (we can accept a Doing-Business-As but it adds a step).
- For urgent invoices under $5k we can process without a PO if you mark the invoice "Non-PO" and copy ap@redwood.ai. For any invoice that will be paid via ACH, please include the 4-digit account suffix in the payment remittance section.

Marcus — can you help validate the W-9 and flag any KYC exceptions? Also looping Laura for contracts visibility (we may add a standard SOW).

On Friday morning (4/6) we plan to create the vendor record — if we have the W-9 and a scanned proof of address by EOD Thursday we should be able to onboard and issue the first PO on Friday.

Thanks,
Neha

Hi all — quick follow-up from tax/finance: 

Received the bank letter and authorization; thanks Alicia. A couple of asks before I can finalise the vendor code: 

1) Please attach the completed W-9 (PDF) with EIN visible. If GrowthPay is a US corporation, W-9 is sufficient; if any entities under GrowthPay are foreign, we need the appropriate W-8s.
2) Beneficial owner declaration or CBP form (simple checkbox form) for entities with >25% foreign ownership.
3) Proof of address (we can accept the bank letter but prefer a recent utility bill or lease in the company name).

Once those are in, I'll create the vendor record and assign Vendor Code: VND-2027-1179. Expect an onboarding confirmation email from ap@redwood.ai with the PO template and payment terms (Net 30 standard).

If you'd like the vendor created earlier to accommodate a close-dated invoice, let me know the invoice number/amount and I'll do an expedited create after W-9 receipt.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Tax & Treasury Analyst | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199
